text:
Maya R: quick design review — compact sparkline interactions for the dashboard. want to decide hover targets, smoothing affordance, and how we show outliers in a dense list. pic: https://img.redwood.com/sparkline-proto (ignore the colors)

Kevin L: love the compact look. main concern is hover hit area — in narrow rows it's hard to hit the line. can we expand the invisible hover zone? :thinking_face:

Tara P: +1 on hit target. also we should avoid hover-only controls for mobile/touch and keyboard users. propose a persistent tiny toggle (icon) next to the metric that opens a mini-overlay with smoothing + outlier options.

Josh C: for accessibility we need keyboard focus on the sparkline itself (tab), pressing enter or space opens the overlay. aria-label should be like: "Sparkline for avg latency, 15m window, press enter for options"

Maya R: thanks. two design tradeoffs: 1) inline micro-toggle (saves clicks, more clutter) 2) overflow menu (clean, extra step). which feels better for power users vs casual viewers?

Kevin L: Leaning overflow menu. keeps table rows compact. micro-toggle could be ok if it's just an icon with a11y label.

Tara P: overflow if we hide it by default. micro-toggle if we expect users to switch smoothing a lot. analytics: do we have telemetry on how often people flip smoothing?

Josh C: not currently for the new compact widget. we can add an event: `sparkline.options.open` and `sparkline.smoothing.set` to gauge.

Maya R: proto suggestion for smoothing toggle text: "Smoothing: Off / Low / High" — short and scannable. tooltip should show exact window length, e.g., "Low = 5-point EMA".

Kevin L: wording nit: use sentence-case in the menu: "Smoothing — low, high" vs all-caps. Also add a tiny info icon that opens a11y copy.

Tara P: outlier handling question: clip vs show jittered dot. clipping hides spikes (good for stable y-axis) but hides real incidents. jitter shows the dot but can overlap. proposal: show outlier dot with thin stroke and label on hover. fallback: show a small red marker for values > 3x median.

Josh C: implementational note: if we render outliers as separate point layer we can make them accessible (focusable) and include a tooltip with exact value and timestamp. code sketch:

```
{
  "type": "sparkline",
  "smoothing": "ema",
  "smoothingWindow": 5,
  "outlierPolicy": "highlight", // options: highlight | clip | hide
  "outlierThreshold": "3x_median",
  "hoverPadding": 6
}
```

Maya R: that looks good. for color we should avoid relying on color alone — add a small patterned outline for outlier points for color-blind users.

Kevin L: agree. pattern + stroke. Also microcopy: the tooltip unit should default to the metric unit (ms, p95, %). we need consistent axis-abbrev rules: we show units on hover and on the column header, but not on every sparkline.

Tara P: accessibility nits: 1) keyboard open/close overlay should announce state via live region; 2) SVG charts need role="img" + aria-labelledby; 3) ensure the focus order doesn't trap users when overlay opens.

DesignBot: auto-check: missing aria attributes detected on current proto: svg missing aria-labelledby, interactive points missing tabindex. See /design/accessibility-checklist.md

Maya R: action items: @Kevin L add telemetry events, @Josh C implement separate outlier layer and keyboard focus, @Tara P write microcopy for smoothing and outlier tooltips, i'll update the prototype with overflow menu and pattern strokes. can we ship a small A/B to 10% to measure toggle usage?

Kevin L: will add events. planning to ship the telemetry in the next deploy window.

Josh C: will mock keyboard interactions and push a branch.

Tara P: I'll draft copy and share a 1-pager.

Maya R: sweet — thanks team. will reconvene after initial telemetry (ETA 2 weeks). :thumbsup:

DesignBot: thread archived after 2 days of inactivity.
